recipes.name: Ham Breakfast Braid
ingredients_raw: 2 (8 ounce) packages refrigerated crescent roll dough

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
Beat milk and cream cheese together until smooth. Mix in eggs, and season with salt and pepper. Heat a lightly oiled skillet over medium-high heat and cook egg mixture until eggs are almost set.

Arrange crescent rolls from one package into a rectangle shape on top of a lightly greased cookie sheet. Place rolls from remaining package along the edges of the two long sides of the rectangle, with the broad half of rolls on top of the first layer of rolls, and the pointed ends extending over the sides of the pan.

Arrange ham in a layer down the center of dough. Spoon cooked egg mixture on top of ham and then sprinkle Cheddar cheese on top of eggs. Bring the corners of the rolls together over cheese to form a “braid” shape.
Bake in the preheated oven for 25 to 30 minutes, until cheese is melted and rolls are golden brown.

raw_recipe.headline: Ham Breakfast Braid
raw_recipe.description: This breakfast braid is a crescent roll dough covered with ham, eggs, and cheese and then formed into a braid shape in this easy-yet-impressive dish.

video.description: Your guests will never guess that the presentation of this breakfast dish is so easy!

review.reviewBody:
Need clearer directions on folding the dough?

I think I can help.

Start by opening and unrolling the crescent roll dough. You will have two rectangles of dough that are scored into triangles.

Place the first rectangle of dough on your cookie sheet so that it is taller than wide. This will be the base for your yummy fillings.

Divide the second piece of dough along the scored lines to form triangles as if you were rolling them for crescent rolls.

Position the triangles along the long sides of the rectangle that serves as your base. You will line them up with the short side of triangle slightly over the dough of the base. The opposite angle should stick out like a baseball pennant/flag.

(To help you imagine this: When this is done, your rectangle of dough might look like a saw with teeth coming out of each side.)

This should yield about 4-6 flags flying off the center base on each side. Press the dough together to hold. Line your fillings on the center base rectangle.

Now, fold each triangle into the center, pulling the dough across the filling and slightly down to meet the rectangle base on the opposite side. Triangles on opposite sides of your base should overlap or criss-cross each other as you fold.

(Visual: Think of how a corset's straps overlap. Or shoelaces.)

Just like a lattice pie, this will yield a crust that looks braided but is merely overlapped.

Wish I could draw you a picture but maybe this will help! :D

We enjoyed it but I made changes to suit our taste as from reading it I thought it would be too bland. I made two braids one with chopped ham, spring onions, mushrooms and a teaspoon of seeded mustard. The other was smoked salmon, spring onions, baby spinach and dill. Also as I'm from Australia I couldn't find the right pastry so used butter puff pastry which worked really well. I'll definitely make again with various ingredients. Thanks for a great starting point.

This came out really good. The use of croissant dough was a good choice because the finished product comes out flaky and lighter than if it used normal bread. I used sliced chorizo instead of ham, and stirred browned ground Italian sausage into the egg mixture about halfway through as the egg began to firm up. One warning: this comes out gi-freaking-normous. For a family of five, I'll cut this recipe in half next time.

Absolutely delicious. I cut the recipe in half as breakfast for two and it still worked beautifully. I also added a few green onions and finished it off with an egg wash before baking. It’s almost embarrassing how easy this is, for how wonderful it turns out! Will definitely be making this again.

If you use parchment paper instead of lightly greasing a cookie sheet, the paper will hold the dough in place more securely, allowing you to create a " straighter/smoother " braid. The parchment paper can also be used to transfer the braid to a fancier serving tray if need be. Also, the bottom of your braid will not be a weird " crunchy/chewy/oily" consistency. Plus, something that I've always experienced when using parchment paper, everything turns out beautiful, golden brown( unless your oven is on it's last leg)!! When I make this recipe I do an egg wash on the braid and sprinkle a little bit of kosher salt on it before baking. Ummm, um. ;)

Hmmmm, This was an awesome way to use leftover ham. After reading reviews, I only added 4 green onions and 1/2 red pepper chopped. I basted the top with an egg and sprinkled sesame seeds. I served it for supper with a salad.... see my picture, this would look great on a table for brunch! 
Oh and I made two at once, my first I cooked at 375 and it was very dark after only 15 min so I cooked the second at 350 for 25 min and it turned out perfect! I posted a picture of a drawing I made for my mom of how I put it together because many seemed to have trouble with it.

I made this for my mom when she came to visit me. It was a huge success! How could you go wrong with crescent rolls, ham, eggs and cheddar! The cream cheese made the eggs so light and fluffy! I took the suggestion of another reviewer and used the crescent sheet. It was much easier to figure out the braid that way. I cut the recipe in half and only had to use one crescent sheet, I just place the sheet long ways on a cookie sheet and gathered the ingredients in the middle. I then sliced from the ingredients out, to create about 6-7 inch wide strips which i wove like a basket over top to lock everything inside! Done perfectly in 25 minutes and oh so good! I plan to make it for my boyfriend this weekend and add in some peppers, onions and mushrooms for a western style ham braid!

I make this recipe every year for a Christmas morning brunch. It's always been a favorite in our family. I found the recipe in one of the Pampered Chef Recipe books years ago. I normally flatten out the two cresent dough rectangles horizontally over a baking sheet. Blend all perforations then flatten out next two crescent dogh rectangles directly below the first. Press together the seams. Dough will overlap the the sides of the baking sheet. But it will resemble a large rectangle placed sideways on the baking sheet. Add ingredients to center of dough and top with cheese. I add chopped green onions to egg mixture and I chop up the sliced breakfast ham steaks. I've also used the chopped ham that comes pre packaged. Then about every 1 and a half inches slice dough from outside edge towards the center of dough about two inches. Do this all the way down one side of dough then repeat down the other side of the dough. Then lift a strip on one side along with a strip of dough on the other side twist a couple of times and lay down. Repeat with each strip till all strips form a sort of a braid look down center of egg mixture. Very good. Even better when its expected only once a year.

Awesome dish! I did not find the instructions hard at all, rather common sense actually. I added onion and bell pepper to the eggs. Now for the super yummy part; I brushed melted butter on the"inside" of the crescent rolls and then generously sprinkled garlic powder over the butter. Shortly before the dish was done I brushed more butter on top and then sprinkled on Italian seasoning. YUM!
I made it vegetarian for my daughter. So I just added mushrooms, green onions, white onions, tomato, bell pepper, and cheese. Then I made some bacon on the side! It was very good and easy to make!

I made this today for Christmas Brunch with leftover ham from last night's feast. I don't like store bought crescent rolls, so I opted to make my own dough. I made the Rapid Mix Sweet Dough found here on Alrecipes yesterday and used half of the dough for this. So, so, so good!!! I also did an extra layer of ham, eggs, and cheese to compensate for any extra doughiness. I baked it for 25 minutes and it came out perfect! 

I would recommend doing an egg-wash on the top once it's all ready for the oven, to bring out that nice golden brown.
We make this for holidays. I added more eggs (4) to fill it out. Added Ham and bacon, extra cheese.
Tasted GREAT and looks so cool. It was surprisingly good leftover too.
Loved it but next time I will add bacon or sausage with. Needs more than just one kinda of meat, besides the eggs
My family loves this! Even my picky teenage who doesn't like eggs!
Fantastic! I used honey butter crescent rolls. Great for Christmas morning.
Was really good.
Perfect recipes! I like that the meat is interchangeable depending on your tastes at the moment. Definitely a keeper!
It was perfect the way it is.
So easy and delicious!
